Swiss Army Bench 0.0.4: a tray icon, starting at sign-in, updates from the tray, and the token out of sight.

- **A tray icon.** Click it to open the app. Right-click shows what is open (tables, Workbench documents), Open the
  Workbench, the blades page, Restart, Start with Windows, and Stop and quit.
- **It starts at sign-in and stays running.** The installer turns this on; untick Start with Windows in the tray (or
  `swissarmybench autostart off`) to stop it. If the server ever stops unexpectedly, the tray restarts it.
- **Updates from the tray.** When a newer version is out, the tray icon gets a dot and its menu starts with
  "Update to X". The app stops, updates and starts again by itself. The grid page and the Workbench show
  "Update available" too. The check asks PyPI for the newest version at start and every six hours, sending nothing
  else; Settings' "Check for updates" turns it off.
- **No token to handle.** The address bar shows just the page's address, and bookmarks and reloads work. A cookie
  that only the app's own pages can send stands in for the token, renewed at each start.
- The blades page's Beta mark shows from the start.

## Update

Stop the running server first (Ctrl+C in its window, or `swissarmybench stop`), then:

```powershell
irm https://github.com/DylanCodyBrown/SwissArmyBench/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex
```

From 0.0.4 on, updates come from the tray's "Update to X".
